title: International Fixed Calendar
intro: The International Fixed Calendar is a proposed reform intended to make monthly dates and weekdays predictable.
structure: Thirteen months of four seven-day weeks contain 364 regular days. Sol is inserted between June and July. Year Day follows the last month; an additional Leap Day occurs in leap years. The proposal treats these special days as outside the regular weekly cycle.
model: The provider implements the Cotsworth 13-month proposal using the proleptic Gregorian year and its leap rule.
example: June 28 is followed by Sol 1 in an ordinary year; after Sol 28 comes July 1.
history: Moses B. Cotsworth promoted the design in the early twentieth century. It was used by some organisations to simplify planning, but was never globally adopted; interruption of the traditional weekly cycle was controversial.
limits: This is a calendar proposal, not a universally used civil chronology. Distinguish intercalary days from ordinary month dates.
